the-line.title: Where the echo is made
the-line.caption: Who talks, who hears, and where the echo is made: the box on the street corner leaks part of the caller’s voice back down the line.

impulse.title: The impulse, moved and scaled
impulse.caption: Top: the impulse δ[n]. Middle: δ[n − 3], the same click 3 samples later. Bottom: 0.8 δ[n], the same click scaled. Small hollow circles are samples that are 0.

impulse-response.title: One click in, h out
impulse-response.caption: The click goes into the box you cannot open. What comes back is the impulse response: 2,000 zeros, then 0.4 and 0.2.

word-as-clicks.title: A word is four clicks
word-as-clicks.caption: Each sample of the word is a click of its own size at its own place. Add the four rows and you get the word back.

copies.title: Each click launches a copy of h
copies.caption: Each click launches a two-bar copy of h, scaled by the click and shifted to start 2,000 samples after it. Add the copies column by column and you get the echo.

convolution-rule.title: The convolution sum, piece by piece
convolution-rule.caption: The same badge number marks the same piece in the formula and in the code. In the formula, x * h names the whole loop, not a product.

flip-slide.title: Flip h, slide it, multiply, add
flip-slide.caption: One output sample at a time: flip h, slide it under the word, multiply each pair, add. Each row is one more step to the right.

smoother-response.title: The smoother, unmasked
smoother-response.caption: First, the smoother’s impulse response: 0.5 and 0.5. Then the tone (dots on a faint curve) and its convolution with 0.5, 0.5 (solid stems). The circled first output is the one lesson 1 left blank.

booster-fails.title: The clipping booster breaks the rule
booster-fails.caption: The old booster’s answer to one click does not predict its answer to another. It is not linear, so convolution does not apply.

pile-of-clicks.title: Why one click is enough
pile-of-clicks.caption: The derivation as a chain. Each arrow names the property it uses.

two-readings.title: Two ways to build the same echo
two-readings.caption: Four copies of h, or two copies of the word: the same echo either way, because x * h = h * x.

canceller.title: The echo canceller
canceller.caption: Follow a word along both paths. The echo and the canceller’s guess reach the minus sign together and cancel, and the far voice passes on.

off-by-one.title: A one-sample slip on “hi”
off-by-one.caption: The echo, the guess one sample late (dashed), and what is left. On “hi” the leftover is bigger than the echo itself.

slip-tones.title: A one-sample slip, tone by tone
slip-tones.caption: The higher the pitch, the more a one-sample slip costs. Above the dashed line, the canceller makes the echo worse.

pointwise.title: Multiplying sample by sample predicts nothing
pointwise.caption: x[n] × h[n] has a zero in every product. Convolution launches a copy of h from every sample instead, and that is the echo.
